cost.description: The direct costs for data generation (laboratory analysis and fish trials) are covered by the PID 41009 grant. However, all data management and long-term storage costs are assumed by the home institution. The institution provides the necessary digital infrastructure, including secure servers with daily backups and access to a certified repository for data sharing, ensuring that no specific additional budget is required for data preservation.

distribution.available_until: The datasets generated during the current study are subject to a temporary embargo, as they constitute a core component of a publication. Consequently, access to the raw and processed data will be restricted to a maximum of 12 months or until the formal publication of the associated peer-reviewed scientific manuscript, whichever comes first. However, the metadata will be made openly available immediately after the completion of the project.

security_and_privacy.description:
During the course of the research project, all data will be stored on local servers maintained and automatically backed up by IRTA/CCMAR. Every night the data will be automatically backed up. The data will be replicated over multiple sites/data centers. Data can be recovered with the help of IRTA/CCMAR services in the event of an incident. Only team members have access to the designated server, limited to the user and supervisor of the project. The storage security is ensured by IRTA/CCMAR services. The IT/Data steward will provide additional advice, as needed, on data storage during the research project. This data storage solution offers secure storage and transfer. 
Data Integrity: File Naming & Versioning: To avoid accidental overwriting, a strict versioning protocol will be used (e.g., BSG-BREAM_GM_GrowthPerformance_v01.csv)

dmp.description: The current project will evaluate the nutritional potential of innovatively produced protein isolate from brewer’s spent grain (BSG) as a functional alternative to soy proteins in gilthead seabream (Sparus aurata) diets. A dose-response feeding trial will be conducted on seabream juveniles by replacing gradient levels of soy protein concentrate (SPC) with BSG protein isolate. The results of this project will provide valuable insights into valorising protein from brewery side streams, contributing to sustainability and circular economy in seabream feed production and farming. The data will be created at the end of feeding trial on growth performance, feed utilization, somatic indices, fillet composition and nutrient retention of seabream juveniles.
